1.why: Reset token is bound to the recovering session via resetHash and only accepted when that session is in the correct stage with a matching digest.

2.why: The reset code is stored only on the issuing session; another user’s session has a different resetHash so the same code does not work for them.

3.why: Password reset updates the account hash and clears recovery fields on the current session only; other sessions in the Map are never invalidated.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS cert/key and refuses to run without them; HSTS is set on responses.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests and passwords with argon2id; session fields themselves are in-memory plaintext, not encrypted at rest.

6.why: Recovery responses use generic account-enumeration-safe wording and do not put private profile fields into the simulated delivery messages.

7.why: Emails, tokens, and passwords are validated with strict allow-lists/length checks; UI inserts values only via text nodes, never as HTML.

8.why: Client only navigates to same-origin paths (e.g. location.origin + /recovery/verify or history.replaceState to /); no user-controlled redirect target is honored.

9.why: There are no HTML email templates; simulated delivery only logs server-generated tokens, not raw user HTML/scripts.

10.why: Authorization secrets, reset tokens, and MFA codes are deliberately written to the client Logs panel and API JSON, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Password is argon2id-hashed, but MFA_CODE is hardcoded in source and the demo password hash also lives in the code.

12.why: A fixed demo account (INTERNAL_ACCOUNT) is embedded and accepted; there is no rejection of default/built-in credentials.

13.why: Channel, reset-verify, login, and MFA paths each increment failure counters and lock out after MAX_RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS within LOCK_TTL.

14.why: Start/login always return the same generic success or error messages with a constant delay, independent of whether the email exists.

15.why: Reset tokens come from randomBytes (base64url), are long enough to be complex, and are bound to the specific recovery session/user flow via resetHash.
